en: Do I love working for Fairfax Industries? No. Does it pay a small fortune? Yes. How do I sleep at night? Like a baby.
What's the point of building toys if you never get to use 'em?
Ready to do some field testing.
Ethics are for scientists that can't think big enough.
So, you need an engineer, huh?
Looks like it's back to the machine shop.
I gotta go back to the lab anyway.
Great. I thought of a new way to weaponize souls in the shower, I need to go to the lab.
You wanna try to win without me? Be my guest.
Wish I could help, this deadline is killing me.
Sorry, the boys in the shop need my help.
Weapons testing is gonna have to wait.
You don't want me to get shot at today? Don't have to tell me twice. Go pick Kevin- Kelvin... w-whatever his name is.

Just wanna get this out of the way: I'm gonna be doing my best to support you, but shit happens and if you end up on the wrong side of a spectral wall... I'm sorry.

No. I'd make a really bad teacher.
I don't know how I do what I do, it just... comes naturally. If I tried to teach someone, it would probably boil down to me saying "Try it again, but don't suck this time!"
Good God. You'd be the Lash of academia.
You say it like that, I kinda wanna give it a try!
No, no. Why do you ask?
I see charm is not one of your talents.

Yeah... that was a little intense.

Honestly, the rest of us were more rattled than he was. I was just a kid freaking out 'cause I thought I was going to lose my job but, Fairfax was surprisingly calm. I don't think he expected Cadenza to last forever. He just wanted to make the most out of an opportunity before legislation caught up. Plus, the guy gets to say he created one of the United States!
When you're someone who cares about legacy as much as he does, that's probably more valuable than money.

How that worked out for you?

First up is asking for an application.

Ohh, so you wanted to have moral superiority over someone you just met.
